subject: Technical deep-dive recap: latency/throughput SLOs & deployment topology
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alice Nguyen <alice.nguyen@acmepayments.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sun, 30 May 2027 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Recap + Next Steps from today's technical deep-dive

Hi Alice / Tom —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap of what we heard and the proposed next steps so we all have the same scope for a POC. Please reply with any corrections.

Key pain points
- Latency spikes in production during peak auth flows (~300-400ms p95 today) that are causing timeout retries in your payment gateway.
- High per-token cost from current managed endpoints that limits model experimentation.
- Need for predictable SLA for fraud & auth inference (business critical).

Goals you shared
- Target p95 inference latency <= 150ms for 512-token sequences in 95% of requests.
- Sustain throughput of ~200 inference requests/sec during peak windows with room to burst to 400rps.
- Keep inference cost <= $0.002 per 1k tokens (target for evaluation).
- Secure, auditable deployment in your VPC with KMS key control and audit logs.

Model & workload requirements (as discussed)
- Primary model: instruction-tuned Llama3-13B (you referred to the internal benchmark).
- Working sequence length: typically 128-512 tokens, occasional 1k token tails.
- Mixed traffic: 70% short inference (<128 tokens), 25% mid (128-512), 5% long (>512).
- Deterministic outputs required for scoring; small sampling not required.

Proposed topology (high level)
- Dedicated GPU pool (multi-A100 class) in us-west region behind smart router for latency routing.
- Autoscaling policy: baseline pool to handle 200rps, rapid scale for bursts to 400rps.
- Prefix/KV caching for repeated context (auth templates) to reduce cost and latency.
- Fallback path: smaller 7B quantized model for best-effort responses if primary pool is constrained.

SLOs & metrics to validate in the POC
- p50/p95/p99 latency for 128/512 tokens
- End-to-end throughput under concurrent load profiles (200rps steady, 400rps burst)
- Token cost estimate and 95% CI based on PoC traffic
- Error rate and fallback frequency

Attachments
- redwood-slo-template.pdf: suggested SLO matrix we can use for acceptance criteria.
- proposed-topology-diagram.png: rough topology we sketched in the call.

Next steps
1) We'll schedule a focused bench test next week to validate latency/throughput. Can you confirm an available 60–90m window on Tue or Wed?
2) Tom: please share a non-sensitive sample of typical requests (anonymized) and your current traffic distribution.
3) We'll provision a short-lived Dedicated test pool and run load profiles; Aditya will lead the test.
4) We'll follow up with a short SLA/contract checklist and a proposed pricing estimate after the bench results.

If that all looks right, I'll lock the call and start provisioning.

Thanks —
Marissa

Subject: Follow-up: bench test plan and topology questions

Hi Alice / Tom —

Quick technical follow-up from my side before we run the bench next Tue. Couple of items that will help us size the pool and tune kernels: feel free to answer inline.

1) Batch sizing: Do you have a target P99 latency requirement that would preclude batching >1 (i.e., do you require strictly single-request per GPU step)? If p99 must be <250ms we may need small batch sizes or prioritized routing for low-latency requests.

2) GPU type: Any restrictions on cloud provider or instance type? We can provision A100 / H100 pools; H100 demonstrates better 13B throughput in our tests but has regional availability differences.

3) KV cache reuse: Will a large portion of your traffic reuse the same prompt prefixes (templates, headers)? If so, enabling persistent KV cache will dramatically reduce repeated compute for long tails.

4) Security: For the VPC deployment, will you want us to manage the KMS keys (customer-managed keys with rotation) or do you require a bring-your-own-key (BYOK) with HSM?

Plan for the bench test (Tue 06/01 10:00 PT)
- 10:00–10:10: quick sync + verification of sample dataset
- 10:10–10:40: steady-state 200rps profile (mix by token length per Marissa's notes)
- 10:40–11:00: 400rps burst profile (10m sustained, with ramp)
- 11:00–11:20: fallback / failure-mode test (simulate capacity constraint)

I'll drop the exact load generator config and the kernel-level logs we capture into the shared folder before the run.

If any of the above contradicts your constraints, please flag.

Thanks —
Aditya
Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference

Thanks all —

Quick answers and final confirmations before the bench:

- Batching: We'll start with small batch sizes (1–2) and use request-type prioritization. For p99 < 250ms we will configure the low-latency routing path to prefer single-request execution.
- GPU: We'll provision H100s in us-west for the initial bench (best throughput for 13B models in our internal tests). If there are availability constraints we'll fallback to A100 with a calibration run.
- KV cache: Please include the anonymized sample so we can quantify prefix reuse; plan is to enable persistent KV cache for the bench.
- KMS: We support both customer-managed keys and BYOK/HSM; for your POC we recommend customer-managed keys with rotation enabled. Aditya will share the integration steps in the shared doc.

Action items
- Alice/Tom: share sanitized sample dataset (target 1k requests) by EOD Monday.
- Aditya: post load-gen config + kernel log capture instructions in the shared Drive link.
- Dylan: I'll loop you in for pricing discussion after bench results.

I'll send the calendar invite for Tue 2027-06-01 10:00 PT and provision the test pool today. Looking forward to the run.
